title: Radian Measure
short: One radian is the angle whose arc equals the radius.
trouble: Students think a radian measure must contain π, so they do not see 2 as an angle.

blocks.html: Degrees split a full turn into $360$ equal parts. That number is a choice people made long ago; nothing about circles forces it. Radians measure an angle with the circle itself. You already know the arc length of a sector. Now flip the idea around: use the arc to measure the angle.
An angle of one radian cuts off an arc exactly as long as the radius. In general an angle in radians counts how many radii fit along its arc: $$\theta = \frac{s}{r}.$$ A full turn is $2\pi$ radians.

Draw the same angle on a small circle and a large one. The sectors are similar, so if the radius doubles, the arc doubles too. The ratio $\frac{s}{r}$ stays the same, so it describes the angle and nothing else. For a full turn the arc is the whole circumference, $2\pi r$, and $\frac{2\pi r}{r} = 2\pi \approx 6.28$. So a little more than six radii wrap around any circle.

blocks.name: pre-radian

opts.task: Drag the point until the arc is exactly $2$ radii long.

blocks.cap: Each colored piece of the arc is one radius long. The numbers $1$ to $6$ mark whole radians; a full turn is $2\pi \approx 6.28$.

blocks.title: From arc and radius
blocks.q: A circle has radius $5$ cm. A central angle cuts off an arc of $15$ cm. What is the angle in radians?
steps: For a feel: $3$ is a little less than $\pi \approx 3.14$, so this is just short of a half turn.

blocks.title: A fraction of a turn
blocks.q: A wheel turns a quarter of a turn. What angle is that in radians?

blocks.title: From angle to arc
blocks.q: An angle of $2$ radians sits at the center of a circle of radius $7$ m. How long is its arc?
steps: Two radians means the arc is two radii long.

blocks.html: Thinking a radian measure must contain $\pi$, so that "$2$" can't be an angle. It can: $2$ radians is the angle whose arc is two radii long, about $114.6^\circ$. The $\pi$ only shows up when the angle is a simple fraction of a full turn, like $\frac{\pi}{2}$ for a quarter turn. Quick check: compare with the landmarks $\frac{\pi}{2} \approx 1.57$, $\pi \approx 3.14$ and $\frac{3\pi}{2} \approx 4.71$ to place any radian measure in its quadrant.
A radian is a length divided by a length, so it has no unit. When an angle is written with no degree sign, like $\theta = 2$, it means radians.
